sourceArticle.title: The Semantic Medallion: Building a Knowledge Graph-Powered Data Catalog
sourceArticle.author: Veronika Heimsbakk

athenaOutput.directive: Establish a self-aware, semantically rich data catalog within the Creative Liberation Engine, leveraging a Knowledge Graph-powered Semantic Medallion architecture to provide unparalleled data discoverability, interoperability, and intelligent reasoning capabilities for all internal and external data assets, fully adhering to Creative Liberation Engine's constitutional principles.
athenaOutput.rationale: The current paradigm of structural data catalogs limits the Creative Liberation Engine's ability to deeply understand and reason over its vast and diverse data landscape. Implementing a Semantic Medallion architecture transforms raw data into a unified knowledge graph, enabling true entity resolution, semantic search, and impact analysis. This strategic shift is critical for the Creative Liberation Engine's self-evolution, advanced AI capabilities, and adherence to Article I (Sovereignty) by building a self-owned and controlled data intelligence layer. It is a novel and necessary capability, not redundant with existing Creative Liberation Engine components.

options.title: Core Creative Liberation Engine Data Fabric Integration
options.description: Fully integrate the Semantic Medallion architecture (Bronze, Silver with IRI minting, Gold Graph with RDF/Ontology) into the Creative Liberation Engine's core data fabric. This involves processing all internal system data and external data feeds through these layers, leveraging a custom Creative Liberation Engine Ontology (IEO) that extends W3C standards like DCAT and SHACL. A dedicated 'IRI Minting Service' and 'Graph Transformation Service' will be developed, storing the resulting Gold Graph in a sovereign, distributed graph database.
options.tradeoffs: High initial architectural complexity and development cost. Requires deep expertise in knowledge graphs, ontology engineering, and distributed graph technologies. Extensive integration work for existing and new data sources.
options.architecture: Develop a custom, scalable 'IRI Minting Service' for globally unique identifiers. Implement a 'Graph Transformation Service' utilizing Python/PySpark for efficient DataFrame-to-RDF conversion, potentially integrating or reimplementing maplib-like functionality. Design and deploy a distributed, self-hosted graph database (e.g., a custom solution or a highly customized open-source stack like JanusGraph/Neo4j) for the Gold Graph. Establish robust SPARQL endpoints for internal agent access and GraphQL for external APIs. Define a comprehensive 'Creative Liberation Engine Ontology (IEO)' extending DCAT, SHACL, and potentially OWL for semantic data modeling.
options.design: Develop a 'Creative Liberation Engine Data Atlas' UI: a highly interactive, visual knowledge graph explorer. Features include dynamic graph visualization with customizable layouts, semantic search with type-ahead suggestions based on the IEO, detailed entity panels showing properties and provenance, and an interactive impact analysis visualization. Include a 'Four Lines of Python' visualizer for template-based graph transformation and a 'Semantic Query Builder' (visual SPARQL constructor). The aesthetic will prioritize clarity, information density, and a consistent visual language for entity types and relationship strengths.

options.title: Federated Semantic Gateway
options.description: Implement a 'Semantic Gateway' as an abstraction layer over existing Creative Liberation Engine data stores and external data sources. This gateway would harvest metadata, mint IRIs, and transform it into a federated knowledge graph using a standardized ontology (DCAT + extensions). The actual data remains in its place, with the gateway providing a unified SPARQL endpoint that translates semantic queries to underlying data store queries via a sophisticated federation engine.
options.tradeoffs: Less direct control over data quality and transformation compared to native integration. Potential query performance overhead due to federation. May not achieve the full 'relationships in the data' benefit if source data isn't deeply transformed.
options.architecture: Develop a 'Metadata Harvester' component with connectors to various Creative Liberation Engine data stores and external APIs. Implement a 'Federated IRI Minting' module for consistent entity identification. Design a 'Metadata-to-RDF Converter' to transform harvested metadata into a federated knowledge graph. Integrate a 'Distributed Query Federation Engine' capable of translating SPARQL queries into native queries for diverse underlying data sources. The federated graph would primarily be a 'metadata graph' rather than a 'data graph'.
options.design: A 'Semantic Data Hub' UI focused on metadata discovery and federated search. This interface would visualize the connections between different data sources through the federated graph. It would offer semantic search with filters for source systems, data lineage views tracing entities back to their origins, and a clear, concise data catalog view. Emphasis would be on highlighting the federated nature of results and providing transparent information about data provenance.

options.title: External Knowledge Graph Service Integration
options.description: Outsource the Gold Graph layer to a managed external knowledge graph service (e.g., AWS Neptune, Google Cloud Knowledge Graph, or a commercial vendor). Creative Liberation Engine agents would perform Bronze and Silver layer processing internally, then push the structured data to the external service for graph storage and querying.
options.tradeoffs: Directly violates Article I (Sovereignty) due to reliance on external, non-owned infrastructure. Introduces vendor lock-in, potential data privacy/security risks, and ongoing subscription costs. Limits deep customization and control over the graph database engine.
options.architecture: Design data pipelines to export Silver layer data in a format compatible with the chosen external knowledge graph service (e.g., RDF, Gremlin, Cypher). Implement secure API integrations for data ingestion and querying with the external service. Focus internal architecture on robust Bronze/Silver processing, with the Gold layer being a simple push/pull mechanism to the external provider.
options.design: The Creative Liberation Engine UI would primarily act as a thin client, integrating via API with the external service's visualization and querying capabilities. This might involve embedding external dashboards or creating bespoke components that mimic the external service's look and feel. The user experience would be dictated by the external provider's offerings, potentially leading to a less cohesive and integrated Creative Liberation Engine aesthetic.

options.title: Data Catalog as an Agent Skill (KEEPER Augmentation)
options.description: Develop a specialized KEEPER sub-agent dedicated to 'Semantic Cataloging' of KEEPER's internal knowledge. This agent would monitor KEEPER's memory ingestion, apply a microcosm of the Silver and Gold Graph transformations, and update a localized graph database (e.g., an embedded RDF store) specific to KEEPER's knowledge domain. This KEEPER sub-agent would then expose an API for semantic queries relevant to its knowledge.
options.tradeoffs: Limited scope; only KEEPER's internal knowledge would be semantically cataloged, not the entire Creative Liberation Engine's data landscape. This could lead to fragmented knowledge if not eventually integrated into a broader system. Requires careful definition of KEEPER's specific ontology.
options.architecture: Implement a self-contained 'KEEPER Semantic Processor' module within KEEPER. This module would include its own 'Mini IRI Minting' and 'Knowledge Graph Transformation' components. Utilize an embedded or lightweight graph database (e.g., Apache Jena TDB, RDFLib, or a small Neo4j instance) for KEEPER's internal Gold Graph. Expose a dedicated internal API for KEEPER's reasoning engine to perform semantic queries against its own knowledge graph.
options.design: KEEPER's internal dashboard would be augmented with a 'Knowledge Graph View' to visualize its interconnected memories and facts. This would be an internal-facing tool for KEEPER's self-management and reasoning, potentially showing reasoning paths and knowledge inference. The UI would be utilitarian, designed for agent insight rather than broad user interaction, focusing on clarity of relationships and fact traceability within KEEPER's domain.

options.title: Progressive Semanticization via Data Contracts
options.description: Introduce 'Semantic Data Contracts' at the Bronze and Silver layers of the Creative Liberation Engine's data ingestion pipelines. Data producers (agents or external systems) would be mandated to provide schema definitions and semantic mappings (e.g., using SHACL or OWL) alongside their data. The Gold Graph would then be built progressively as these contracts are fulfilled, enforced by a 'Contract Validation Service' and a 'Semantic Schema Registry'.
options.tradeoffs: Requires a significant operational shift and enforcement mechanism for data producers. Initial overhead in defining and standardizing contracts. Full graph construction depends on widespread adoption and compliance with contracts.
options.architecture: Develop a 'Semantic Schema Registry' to store and manage all defined data contracts (SHACL shapes, OWL ontologies, RDFS schemas). Implement a 'Contract Validation Service' at the Bronze/Silver boundary to ensure incoming data conforms to its declared semantic contract. Integrate 'Contract-Driven Graph Transformation' logic, where the Gold Graph generation is directly informed and guided by the semantic mappings specified in the contracts. This pushes semantic definition upstream, enhancing data quality at the source.
options.design: Develop a 'Data Contract Management' UI where Creative Liberation Engine agents or developers can define, validate, and publish semantic data contracts. This interface would include a visual contract editor for defining IRIs, properties, and relationships, along with real-time schema visualization and validation feedback. A dashboard would display the compliance status of various data sources against their contracts. A 'Semantic Data Contract Marketplace' could allow agents to discover and subscribe to data streams based on their rich semantic descriptions.
